title: Random example matrix outcome
statement: Let $X=\{-1,1\}^n$, let $f:X\to\{-1,1\}$ be a target function, let $I$ be a finite set, and let $m,w$ be natural numbers. Given an array of inputs $x_{k,i}\in X$ indexed by $k\in I$ and $1\leq i\leq m$, apply a specified function to the array of labeled pairs $(x_{k,i},f(x_{k,i}))$. The resulting outcome is that function’s value together with the cost $(|I|m,0,|I|m+w)$, recording random examples, membership queries, and local computation steps in that order.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a function from $\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\{-1,1\}$
The output function accepts arrays indexed by $I$ and $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ of input-label pairs
